chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from a man from our companions, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Isma'il, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave whom he had sexual relations with, and she would go out for his needs. She became pregnant, and he feared that the child might be his. What should he do? Should he sell the female slave and the child? He said: He sells the female slave and does not sell the child, nor does he bequeath to him anything from his inheritance.

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual relations with her
key_terms.يُورِثُهُ: He bequeaths to him / He inherits from him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a concubine and her child if the father fears paternity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of 'Umm al-Walad' (concubine who bears a child), establishing that while the father retains ownership of the mother to sell her, the child remains free and distinct from the father's direct lineage for inheritance purposes. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the child does not automatically inherit from the father unless specified, differentiating this status from legitimate marital offspring and emphasizing the separation of the mother's servitude from the child's freedom.
